notes: Three DSH lifetimes run in sequence: clean /exit after a completed turn, SIGKILL while idle in ready, and SIGKILL during a deliberately long turn. Every birth selects a real session-UUID row and every later phase is pinned to that variant, so proc-<PID> pre-sessions and neighboring variants cannot satisfy the checks. Variant 3 forbids a ready transition before exit, which proves the kill occurred mid-turn rather than after an unexpectedly fast completion. Metric observations are intentionally omitted because the final variant is killed before assistant usage is durable; this cell asserts lifecycle only, matching the claudecode and Muse sibling specs. PID binding order was corrected per #1985, 'feat(onboard): record deepseek-harness/session-end': the live DSH recording shows turn/start activity before lock-based pid_discovered for each lifetime.

text: Variant 1: the first real DSH UUID session appears in ready
Variant 1: the no-op prompt drives ready to working
Variant 1: PID binds through session.lock after the first activity
Variant 1: completed turn/end returns the session to ready
Variant 1: clean /exit flushes DSH and terminates the process after the session is ready
Variant 2: restart creates a second real DSH UUID session in ready
Variant 2: the no-op prompt drives ready to working
Variant 2: PID binds through its new session.lock after the first activity
Variant 2: completed turn/end returns the session to ready before the idle kill
Variant 2: SIGKILL while idle removes the ready session without a post-turn state change
Variant 3: restart creates a third real DSH UUID session in ready
Variant 3: the long prompt drives ready to working
Variant 3: PID binds through its new session.lock after the first activity
Variant 3: SIGKILL lands while the long turn is still working; no terminal ready transition occurred first
